finding: The normative definition of `blocking` is "no surviving non-PASS row carries a blocking severity", but the spec never states WHICH of error|warning|info are blocking. The sentence leans on "the same terms" as review_converge_on, yet review is over a different vocabulary: internal/cli/review.go:1973 defines the review rule as "critical or high severity under review_converge_on=blocking". There is no critical/high in an audit row and no mapping is given. An implementer must infer error-only from a parenthetical in the §2.1 table ("r2, r3 carry zero error") and from §7 test 2 (warning and info count clean), which is inference from examples, not a definition.
suggestion: State the set literally in §2: under blocking a non-PASS row blocks iff its severity is error; warning and info do not block. Add a named engine predicate (the audit twin of ValidReviewConvergeOn / the review blocking-severity set) so the setter, the record path and the status path read one definition.

finding: The safety argument "The field it reads already exists and is already validated ... audit_schema.go rejects a row that omits it. Nothing new is asserted by the agent being measured" does not hold. internal/cli/audit_schema.go is a prompt RENDERER: renderAuditOutputSchema writes the sentence "severity: field MUST exist; null for PASS, one of error|warning|info for PARTIAL or FAIL" into the auditor prompt. It rejects nothing. The only row validation on the record path is invalidCategoryRows in internal/cli/audit_record.go, which checks `category` and nothing else, and whose own doc comment records this exact failure mode for category: tp "renders the enum into every auditor prompt ... in words that promise unknown values are rejected -- and then never looked at what came back". So a non-PASS row can reach the permanent round file with severity absent, null, or an arbitrary string, and the whole convergence decision would rest on it.
suggestion: Either add severity validation to the record path in this release (mirroring invalidCategoryRows: collect every offending line, abort with one message) and say so in §2 and §7, or state the fallback the blocking predicate applies to a non-PASS row whose severity is missing/null/unknown. Fail-closed (treat it as blocking) is the only choice that cannot be exploited by the agent being gated; whichever is chosen, name it, because the release ships nothing safe without it.

finding: No surface contract is given for the new field. §7 test 1 requires it to resolve "through the documented precedence", but nothing in this document documents a precedence or names a single surface. review_converge_on touches at least: engine/projectconfig.go (the allowed project-field set and its validator), cli/set.go (the settable workflow field list plus its enum branch), cli/set_project.go, cli/config.go (--resolved), cli/config_extract.go, cli/validate_project.go, engine/unattended.go (whether a raise/change is a user-approved decision under TP_UNATTENDED), and the consuming commands. v0.31.1 exists precisely because review_converge_on shipped missing config --extract and validate --project. Without the list, this release repeats that miss and the gap is invisible until a later cycle.
suggestion: Add a §2 subsection enumerating every surface audit_converge_on must appear on, with the precedence spelled out (CLI > env > task override > project config > built-in), and state whether it is a TP_UNATTENDED-guarded decision. One list makes it decomposable into one task per surface and makes the omission checkable.

finding: §5 is titled as a defect this release must fix, says "What this release must decide", and then does not decide it: it offers "The candidate shapes, neither chosen here" -- a role-scoped convergence set (converge_roles) or a --check that reports the shipping predicate with the all-roles count demoted to advisory. These are not two spellings of one change; they differ in the config surface, the payload shape, and what exit 0 means. I cannot open a commit against this section. The acceptance sentence at the end (a fixture where the conformance role is clean while another role has open non-FAIL rows must reach exit 0) is satisfied by both shapes and by shapes neither names, so it does not close the gap either.
suggestion: Choose one shape and specify it (field name, default, payload keys, exit-code table), or move §5 to Non-Goals with a pointer to the version that takes it. A section whose requirement is "decide the design" cannot be decomposed and will be re-derived by hand in the implementation phase, which is exactly what the section complains about.

finding: Change (2), "A PASS carrying such a statement is an unresolved item for convergence, not a clean one", requires a machine-readable marker on the row, and §5a specifies none. engine.AuditRowIsPass is byte-exact (status == "PASS", "no trimming, no case folding"), so nothing in the row as it exists today can carry the statement; §5a explicitly declines to touch the checklist, and change (1) is only a wording change to the emitted brief, which produces prose in `notes` at best. Unspecified: the field name, whether renderAuditOutputSchema must require it, whether it is validated at record, whether such a row carries a severity (and therefore whether it blocks under audit_converge_on=blocking from §2), and which of the five AuditRowIsPass consumers must stop treating it as clean.
suggestion: Specify the carrier explicitly -- e.g. a nullable `unaddressed` object with the statement plus the recommendation change (1) forces -- its schema row, its validation, its severity semantics, and the predicate change (state it as a new engine predicate rather than as a change to AuditRowIsPass, whose doc comment forbids drift). Also reconcile with §6 item 5: deferring "a fourth row status" to spec/0.49.0.md §5 while requiring a PASS row to count as unresolved is the same need answered twice, in two releases, in two shapes.

finding: §5b measures the defect well and then states the fix as an opinion: "The cheap answer is that a recorded round should carry forward the roles it did not receive, marked as not-run rather than dropped". As a requirement it is missing every decidable part: where the expected role set comes from (the active corpus, the round roles_hash, or the previous round role_streaks), what the not-run marker is called and what an entry looks like in role_streaks, whether a round missing a role can still be clean: true, whether consecutive_clean and spec_coverage_clean_rounds freeze or reset for a carried-forward role, and what happens when the corpus itself changed between rounds (engine.ReadAuditRoundRows already drops a whole round on a differing roles_hash, so the two rules can disagree about the same round). There is also no §7 test for it.
suggestion: Promote it to a Mechanism block with the same rigour §3 and §4 get: the source of the expected role set, the literal marker, the effect on clean, on consecutive_clean, on spec_coverage_clean_rounds, and the interaction with the roles_hash rule. Add the test: a one-role round recorded against a three-role corpus leaves the other two streaks at their prior values and does not advance them.

finding: The reset names exactly one counter -- "resets consecutive_clean to zero". Every other streak the loop stores is left untouched: role_streaks[].consecutive_clean and spec_coverage_clean_rounds (engine/rolestreaks.go). §5 and §5b of this same spec establish that the shipping rule people actually use reads spec_coverage_clean_rounds, so under §4 as written an agent can amend the spec mid-audit, lose the counter nobody ships on, and keep the counter everybody ships on -- which is the §1 hazard verbatim. Two further gaps: the first recorded round has no previous round to compare against (no rule stated), and the comparison is against the PREVIOUS ROUND spec_hash, so a spec that moves and moves back between two records is invisible.
suggestion: State the full reset scope: name every streak the change zeroes (or state explicitly which survive and why). Define the first-round case. If the intent is to catch the §1 case ("the spec hash changed twice mid-audit"), say whether --record compares against the previous round hash or against the live spec on disk -- they catch different things.

finding: "and says so in the payload" (§4) and "reports the reset on the machine-readable surface" (§7 test 6) name no key, no value, and no command. tp audit has two machine-readable surfaces (--record and --status), and the reset is a fact both would want. An implementer will invent a key name; a later cycle will find it undiscoverable, exactly as §5 describes for the --check gap.
suggestion: Name the key and its value (e.g. streak_reset_reason: spec_changed with the two hashes), say which surfaces carry it (--record, --status, or both), and say whether it changes the exit code of anything. Then test 6 becomes assertable as written.

finding: §3 scopes the change to "the round finding count" only. But AuditRowIsPass has five call sites and its own doc comment makes the identity load-bearing: "This is byte-for-byte the predicate the audit record path applies ... it must stay identical to it: were the two to drift, the per-role open counts and the round stored findings would disagree about the same rows." The consumers are cli/audit_record.go:248 (the count), engine/rolestreaks.go:138 (per-role open + streaks), engine/divergence.go:137 (the divergence signal), and engine/nextunits.go:188 (which ALREADY excludes disposed rows via rowDisposed). Excluding wontfix/duplicate in the count alone breaks the stated invariant; excluding it everywhere silently changes divergence, the one signal §1 credits with catching this class.
suggestion: Enumerate the consumers and state for each whether the disposition exclusion applies. In particular say what divergence should see: an accepted-backlog row is precisely the input divergence was built to notice, so hiding it there may be the wrong half of the fix.

finding: A disposition is written by tp audit --resolve into the results NDJSON, which normally happens AFTER the round was recorded; the round finding count is frozen at --record time. §3 does not say whether the exclusion is applied when the round is recorded (so a row accepted afterwards never unblocks the round it was found in -- the field-cycle scenario §3 exists to fix) or recomputed from the current results files at --status/--check time (which is what the review side does: review_status.go recomputes survivors under the "current resolution" state). §7 test 5 passes under either reading, so the ambiguity survives the test.
suggestion: State the evaluation time explicitly and mirror review if that is the intent. If it is recompute-at-status, say what --record stores in findings so the stored number and the reported number are not silently different quantities.

finding: The table cell "v0.36.0 | 7 and open" is stale, and it understates the case against the default it is cited for. Counted just now over spec/.tp-review/0.36.0/audit-round-*.ndjson there are THIRTEEN recorded audit rounds, and non-PASS error rows appear in rounds 1 (8), 7 (3), 12 (2) and 13 (2). §5 of this same spec tabulates rounds 10-13 and §2.0a discusses rounds 12 and 13, so the document contradicts itself about how long that cycle ran. Everything else I could re-derive holds: v0.35.0 is 3 error / 22 warning / 17 info as §1 says, blocking converges at round 3 and all at round 9 under audit_clean_rounds 2, and v0.36.0 under all has still not converged at round 13.
suggestion: Refresh the cell to 13 and restate the argument on the fuller data: under blocking + 2 clean rounds v0.36.0 would have closed at round 3 and then missed error rows in rounds 7, 12 AND 13, not only round 7. Since §2.1 tells decomposition this is the one decision with a recorded argument against it, the decomposer needs the correct size of that argument.

finding: Test 4 pins two literals (blocking converges at round 3, all at round 9) against the live spec/.tp-review/0.35.0/ round files in the working tree. Those files are writable state, and this very release makes them semantically live: §3 lets tp audit --resolve write a wontfix/duplicate disposition into a recorded row and have it change a finding count. So dispositioning any old v0.35.0 row -- or any future repair that rewrites those rounds -- silently moves a gate expectation. CLAUDE.md already treats spec/.tp-review/ as state the suite must not disturb (check-suite-state.sh hashes it before and after).
suggestion: Copy the nine round files into a frozen testdata fixture and replay against that, or derive the expectation from the fixture rather than asserting 3 and 9 as literals. Keep the recorded-history claim in the spec as prose; do not make a mutable corpus a gate input.

finding: Both candidate shapes lean on "the conformance role" -- converge_roles "defaulting to the conformance role", and a --check reporting "conformance-role streak plus no-FAIL". tp has no notion of a conformance role: roles are user-defined files under .tp/auditors/, per-spec activation has existed since v0.32.0, and spec_coverage_clean_rounds is already a signal keyed to one literal role name that a corpus need not contain. The spec never says how the role is identified, nor what --check does in a corpus with no spec-coverage role (every field repo that ejects or renames the corpus), nor what happens when the named role is deactivated for this spec.
suggestion: State the identification rule and the fallback: an explicit configured role list with no name-based default, or a documented default of spec-coverage plus the defined behaviour when it is absent or inactive (fall back to all roles, or refuse with an exit code and hint). This is the part a field repo hits first.

finding: The error paths carry no exit codes or hints, which the review twin does specify by having two distinct ones. For review_converge_on: a bad literal at the setter exits 2 with engine.ReviewConvergeOnHint (cli/set.go, cli/set_project.go), and a resolved-but-invalid STORED value at a consuming command exits ExitValidation=1 with the same hint (cli/review_record.go:49, cli/review_status.go:40). §7 test 1 covers only "an illegal literal is refused with the hint naming both legal values" -- the setter half -- so the stored-value half of the twin would ship untested and undefined. Nothing in §3, §4, §5a or §5b names an exit code either.
suggestion: Add an exit-code line to §2: bad literal at set / set --project exits 2; an invalid stored audit_converge_on at tp audit --record / --status exits 1; hint text is the shared AuditConvergeOnHint naming blocking and all. Add the second case to test 1.

finding: The spec never says whether the emitted auditor prompt learns the active policy. The review side does: cli/review.go:1969-1973 renders one blockingRule sentence describing BOTH settings into the prompt. Two consequences if audit does not. The auditor keeps assigning severity with no idea it now gates the release, which is the moment severity stops being an unforced label and starts being one the measured agent has an incentive to lower -- the exact objection §2 uses to keep scope deferred. And §2.0a asks for a role that can be told to re-examine its own prior reasoning rather than stop at round 3, which is a prompt change nobody has been assigned.
suggestion: State whether the audit prompt carries the stop rule, and if it does, render it for both settings the way review does (one sentence, policy-independent, so prompt text does not vary with a workflow field). Say explicitly whether §2.0a caveat produces any prompt change in THIS release or is only a note pointing at spec/0.49.0.md §1c.

finding: §2 and §3 compose in a way neither states, and the composition can disarm the release safety property. §2 blocking is a predicate over "surviving non-PASS rows"; §3 removes wontfix/duplicate rows from the count. Nothing says what happens to an ERROR-severity row dispositioned wontfix. On the natural reading it stops blocking, so an operator -- or, under tp run, the agent being gated -- converges the phase by labelling the one blocking row accepted. That is precisely the objection §2 cites to defer scope for a fourth time: "a self-declared label that gates a release is strictly worse than over-counting, because the agent whose work is being gated writes the label". A disposition is exactly such a label, and this release makes it gate.
suggestion: Decide and state the order and the limit. Options worth naming: an error-severity row cannot be dispositioned wontfix (refuse at --resolve with exit 2); or it can, but the round reports it under a distinct key (accepted_blocking) and --check still refuses; or dispositions are excluded only for non-error severities. Also state whether tp audit --resolve is a user-approved decision under TP_UNATTENDED, since v0.35.0 fences the other four.

finding: The default is stated as a requirement in §2 ("Default. blocking, matching review_converge_on") and then re-opened in §2.1: "whichever default ships" and "Decomposition should treat the default as the one decision in this release with a recorded argument against it". An implementer writing the built-in constant needs one answer. As written I cannot tell whether blocking is the specified default or a proposal the decomposition phase is being asked to settle, and the two produce different code, different config defaults, and a different meaning for every existing repo that upgrades.
suggestion: Pick the default in §2 and keep §2.1 as the recorded argument against it, or state explicitly that the default is `all` (behaviour-preserving on upgrade) with blocking opt-in. Either is buildable; the current pair is not. If the intent is for the operator to decide at decomposition, say so as an escalation rather than as a stated default.

finding: §7 covers §2 (tests 1-4), §3 (test 5) and §4 (tests 6-8). §5, §5a and §5b -- the three sections new since v0.36.0 shipped, and the three carrying the most undefined mechanism -- have no test. §5 embeds one acceptance sentence in its own body which satisfies both of its unchosen shapes; §5a and §5b have none at all. Without acceptance, these sections cannot be turned into tasks with a definition of done, and on tp own workflow they would be closed on prose evidence.
suggestion: Once §5, §5a and §5b state a mechanism, add a test for each to §7: the §5 fixture already written in that section, a §5a fixture where a PASS row carrying the new statement keeps a round unclean and one without it does not, and the §5b fixture where a one-role round leaves absent roles streaks unchanged and does not report clean. If any of the three is not ready to specify, move it out of this release rather than shipping it untested.
